propositions: Newly added hard-fail CI gates break in-flight branches and branches predating the gate because the code-review gate has no criterion checking whether a branch created before a pipeline change would now fail.

The project.ci-gate-compat advisory criterion must ask whether a pipeline/gate-configuration change introduces a hard-fail step or required gate with no if-present/grandfather guard, in CI-vendor-agnostic language.

Project code-review criteria are activated unconditionally without reference to applies_to globs, so applies_to gating must be implemented in gate_dispatch._activated_code_review_project_criteria and registry.py to filter by changed files.

A project must be able to override applies_to globs via a config key (code_review.ci_config_globs) declared in the criterion's applies_to_config_key pointer, so unusual pipelines are declared rather than enumerated by rebar.

The criterion's applies_to must declare CI-vendor-neutral glob patterns for eight systems (GitHub Actions, Jenkins, GitLab CI, CircleCI, Azure Pipelines, Buildkite, Bitbucket Pipelines, Drone) so adding a new CI system requires only adding a glob, not editing code.
